title: 방향과 회전 행렬 · 추가 비교와 첫 원문 후보

scenes.title: 새 비교 예시의 순서
lines: After comparing the orientations of a flying character and a bicycle, we will apply the same frame-based reasoning to an assembled aircraft and component placement.

scenes.title: 자전거에서도 위치와 자세를 나눕니다
lines: We can also see the distinction between direction and orientation on a bicycle.
Descenders is a cycling game about riding mountain trails and making jumps.
First separate the changing position on a winding trail from the bicycle leaning.
In the next jump, the wheels turn upside down and then face downward again before landing.
Travel direction alone cannot describe that inversion, so we need to record both the front and the top of the bicycle.

scenes.title: 앞과 날개를 함께 읽는 비행 자세
lines: Now we will use an assembled aircraft in Trailmakers to see what the axes mean.
In this game, you build vehicles from parts and drive or fly them.
After takeoff the wings tilt; from the next viewpoint they return to nearly level.
The red line marks the front of the aircraft, and the blue line connects the two sides of its wings.
Reading both lines helps us distinguish inclination that the forward direction alone misses.
The camera also moves, so these screen lines are observation guides; our earlier ninety-degree calculation is a separately defined mathematical example.

scenes.title: 비행 자세에서 부품 배치 자세로
lines: Once we can record the orientation of a flying object, we can reason in the same way about a component we are about to place.
In Space Engineers, parts are assembled to build spacecraft.
The translucent component inside the green box is a preview that has not yet been placed.
Compare the shot of the small component turning upright and sideways with the shot of a solid component placed in the chosen orientation.
A change of size selection is separate from rotation.
Here we choose a placement orientation rather than fly an aircraft, but the shared principle is to record the object axes in one reference frame.

scenes.title: 21a 첫 원문 보정 후보
lines: Knowing a starting and target orientation does not automatically give a valid intermediate orientation.
